items.claim: A JWT exists to establish authenticity, not to hide data, so every claim in the token is readable and rewritable by the client and only signature verification should be trusted.
items.body:
A JWT exists to establish authenticity, not to hide data, so every claim in the token is readable and rewritable by the client and only signature verification should be trusted.

HackTricks reference: jwt (https://kathan19.gitbook.io/howtohunt/jwt-attack/jwt.md)
items.disproof: The token is encrypted so its claims are unreadable without the key, or altering a claim makes the server reject the signature.

sources.quote:
So the integrity and authenticity of the token can be verified by other parties involved.
* The goal of using JWT is not to hide data, but to ensure the data's authenticity.
If more than one kind of JWT can be issued by the same issuer, the validation rules for those JWTs MUST be written such that they are mutually exclusive, rejecting JWTs of the wrong kind.
In such cases, the relying party or application MUST validate the audience value, and if the audience value is not present or not associated with the recipient, it MUST reject the JWT.

items.claim: The JWT header is client-readable and names the algorithm used for signing, which makes the alg value the first field to inspect and the first one to tamper with.
items.body:
The JWT header is client-readable and names the algorithm used for signing, which makes the alg value the first field to inspect and the first one to tamper with.

HackTricks reference: jwt (https://kathan19.gitbook.io/howtohunt/jwt-attack/jwt.md)
items.disproof: The server ignores the alg stated in the header and validates only tokens it verifies against its own pinned key, so changing alg has no effect.
